Describe a three-dimensional plot for a document

Source: R/knitr-3d.R
alt_text_3d.Rd

Describes the layers, mapped variables and initial camera. An explicit labs(alt = ...) takes precedence. Review the description when the plot communicates a finding that needs words beyond its mapped variables.

Usage

alt_text_3d(plot)

Arguments

plot

A ggplot with coord_3d().

Value

One character string.

Details

In knitr and Quarto documents, view3d = TRUE in a chunk selects view_3d() for HTML output. PDF and Word receive a static plot drawn with the vector scene backend. The chunk's fig.alt overrides the generated description. Widget dimensions follow fig.width and fig.height in inches at 96 pixels per inch.

The chunk option raster3d keeps a static plot of dense geometry small: TRUE draws its vector-backend panels with backend_3d("hybrid", rasterise = "surfaces"), which draws the faces of every depth-tested or rear-pane layer into one image while paths, points, axes, panes, grid lines and text stay vector graphics. A number is a file size in bytes: the plot is drawn as vector graphics and, while the file exceeds that size, again with rasterise = "surfaces" and then with rasterise = "all", which also draws paths and points into the image; the smallest file is kept. The image has the chunk's dpi pixels per inch, which knitr multiplies by fig.retina for HTML output: the density of a raster figure from the same chunk. Panels with another backend are left as they are. The same applies to patchwork compositions that contain ggplot3d plots.

For a raster scene saved with ggplot2::ggsave(), set both backend_3d("raster", dpi = 300) and ggsave(..., dpi = 300) for a 300 dpi image. The backend dpi controls scene sampling at its physical panel size; the device dpi controls the saved image's pixel dimensions.

Examples

p <- ggplot2::ggplot(mtcars, ggplot2::aes(wt, mpg, z = hp)) +
  geom_point_3d() + coord_3d(azimuth = 40, elevation = 25)
alt_text_3d(p)
alt_text_3d(p + ggplot2::labs(alt = "Fuel economy, weight and horsepower."))
